legacy.note: sum of the per-query medians (A100-study comparability); arithmetic, never combined with geometric means
unstable_coverage.note: excluded by A1 (unstable coverage); not an estimate. Amendment A1: a coverage outcome observed in some rounds but not others for the same (engine, suite, scale, query) is excluded from every contrast, per-query and suite-level, in all rounds; the raw per-round values are listed here for transparency only.
plan_variability.note: Descriptive. The final adaptive plan of every Spark trial (plans/<query>-<phase>-<trial>.txt) is normalized (expression, plan, stage and lore ids removed) and hashed; a cell is listed when its trials do not all end in the same plan. Medians, estimates and intervals are unchanged by this section: every measured trial still enters its cell's median as designed.

secondary.gpu_memory.measure_note.polars: nvidia-smi device memory of the worker process, sampled during the timed action. cudf-polars allocates through an RMM async pool that keeps freed blocks (release threshold 90% of the device), so the value is the pool's high-water mark in that session so far, not the working set of the query: it never falls within a session (see high_water_check) and an upper bound on what the query needs
secondary.gpu_memory.measure_note.spark_: the largest device allocation a single task reported (RAPIDS task accumulator gpuMaxDeviceMemoryBytes, Spark event log) among the tasks launched inside the action; not a simultaneous total over concurrent tasks. The nvidia-smi samples (max_bytes, ...) are the worker process tree's device memory when the action was sampled; they are constant within a session in only 0 of 32 sessions, so on this host they are not a fixed pool reservation (the first sampled action of a session reads 177.8 GiB and the minimum over the later actions 8.3 GiB, medians over sessions) and they are not task-level usage
secondary.gpu_memory.note: max_bytes / median_bytes / min_bytes are the nvidia-smi samples of the worker process tree during the timed action (worker peak_gpu_memory_bytes); maximum over the 3 measured trials, then over rounds; a sampled peak can miss short transients. What the sample means differs by engine: see measure / measure_note, and the task_reported blocks for Spark GPU
secondary.energy.definition: GPU board energy proxy = mean nvidia-smi power.draw over the session window x process wall time; CPU and host power are not included, and CPU-only engines show the idle GPU draw
secondary.gpu_telemetry.meta.label: descriptive telemetry; not a pre-registered contrast; no causal claim
secondary.gpu_telemetry.meta.definition: For each GPU engine, suite and scale: the nvidia-smi samples (utilization.gpu, utilization.memory, power.draw, clocks.current.sm) that fall inside the measured actions of the accepted rounds, pooled over queries, trials and rounds. idle_fraction is the share of samples with utilization.gpu below 10% (equal to the share of action wall time at uniform sampling). utilization.gpu is nvidia-smi's share of the sample period in which at least one kernel was executing, not SM occupancy. Descriptive; not a pre-registered contrast; no causal claim.
secondary.gpu_telemetry.meta.power_limit: nvidia-smi -q, Current Power Limit of the first GPU
secondary.gpu_telemetry.meta.resolution_: nvidia-smi is sampled about every 200 ms, so an action of 1 s holds about 5 samples and the first and last sample of an action are partly outside it; actions shorter than 1 s (most SF1 actions) are left out of every statistic and counted in n_actions_excluded_short
exploratory.e1.meta.label: exploratory (post-hoc; not in the locked design §9)
exploratory.e1.meta.interval: Welch-type 95% interval on the log scale: the CPU times come from the side-study sessions and the GPU times from the main rounds, different sessions in different rounds, so the two sets of per-round values are unpaired (Welch-Satterthwaite df); no interval with fewer than two rounds on either side
exploratory.e1.meta.definition: time of the Polars CPU side-study sessions / time of the GPU side of the main rounds, per (suite, scale, query); above 1 means the GPU side was faster. The suite value is the same estimator over the per-round geometric mean of the queries timed in every round on both sides. This is post-hoc: not pre-registered, not part of the locked design (section 9), never mixed into C1-C4 or the crossover verdict.
exploratory.e1.meta.reason: no side study with two Polars versions
exploratory.e4.meta.label: exploratory (post-hoc; not in the locked design §9)
exploratory.e4.meta.denominator: best GPU engine per query and main round (polars_gpu or spark_gpu)
exploratory.e4.meta.interval: Welch-type 95% interval on the log scale: the CPU times come from the side-study sessions and the GPU times from the main rounds, different sessions in different rounds, so the two sets of per-round values are unpaired (Welch-Satterthwaite df); no interval with fewer than two rounds on either side
exploratory.e4.meta.definition: time of the Polars CPU side-study sessions / time of the GPU side of the main rounds, per (suite, scale, query); above 1 means the GPU side was faster. The suite value is the same estimator over the per-round geometric mean of the queries timed in every round on both sides. This is post-hoc: not pre-registered, not part of the locked design (section 9), never mixed into C1-C4 or the crossover verdict.
exploratory.e4.meta.reason: no side study with two Polars versions

a100_vs_h100.meta.definition: time on A100 / time on H100 for the same GPU engine, query and scale; above 1 means the H100 host was faster. The A100 study is a single session per cell (no rounds), so the interval reflects the H100 round-to-round variation only. Hosts differ in GPU, vCPU count, RAM and software versions: not an equivalent comparison. The A100 side is the previous study's saved evidence (see study.label and study.differences), not the A100 campaign.

a100_vs_h100.study.plan_variability.note: Descriptive. The final adaptive plan of every Spark trial (plans/<query>-<phase>-<trial>.txt) is normalized (expression, plan, stage and lore ids removed) and hashed; a cell is listed when its trials do not all end in the same plan. Medians, estimates and intervals are unchanged by this section: every measured trial still enters its cell's median as designed.
